facts.text: Hilham was founded in 1797 by Dartmouth graduate Moses Fisk, who believed the site marked the geographic center of the United States at the time.
Fisk platted Hilham with roads radiating north, south, east, and west, hoping the town would become a national crossroads for travel and commerce.
In 1806, Fisk established one of the Southeast’s first female academies in Hilham, chartered by the Tennessee General Assembly for women’s education.
The Moses Fisk House, now at the park entrance, stands as a tangible link to Hilham’s pioneering past and the town’s early surveyor‑founder.
Hilham’s park preserves a historic Native American landmark—a large sandstone boulder that once served as a boundary marker—and offers over eight miles of trails with views of Dale Hollow Lake.
The town’s name comes from “Hamlet on the Rill,” reflecting its position near a small stream on the Cumberland Plateau.
